title: AI Food and Drink Product Videos | AIVideosUGC
description: Turn one food or drink photo into a pour, a first bite, or a shelf shot. Download watermark-free clips for listings, social feeds, and paid ads.
h1: AI Food and Drink Product Videos for the Pour and the Plate
lead: Hungry shoppers decide quickly. One package photo can become a pour, a first bite, or a shelf moment without booking a kitchen.
card: Pours, plates, and package scenes from one food photo.

faq.q: Will the ingredient list and nutrition panel look right?
faq.a: Do not rely on the image for that. Small print may not match the real package. Allergens, ingredients, and nutrition facts should always come from the real label.

faq.q: Can I show a pour if I only have a photo of the can?
faq.a: Yes. Describe the glass, the ice, and the color of the liquid. Name the texture in plain words so the pour stays close to the real drink.

faq.q: How long should a food clip be?
faq.a: 6 or 10 seconds covers one pour or one bite. Use 15 seconds for two moments, or 30 seconds for a longer serve. Credits are 24, 40, 60, and 120. A failed job returns its credits.

faq.q: Should I spray the can for a cold look?
faq.a: No. Ask for condensation in the description, then photograph the dry can in side window light with fingerprints wiped off.

faq.q: Can I run the clips as paid food and drink ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloads are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use, including paid ads. Keep nutrition, allergen, and ingredient claims on the real package.

faq.q: Do I need a creator or a filming kitchen?
faq.a: Not for these clips. Hands and the setting are generated from your package photo. A real tasting, or a recipe you must show exactly, still needs a real shoot.
Video frames are 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, and 3:4. A vertical 9:16 fits a phone feed. A square still fits many listings.

faq.q: What should the scene keep visible?
faq.a: Keep the package shape and the main label area recognizable, and end on the full product when you can. Do not ask the clip to invent a flavor that is not in the photo.

steps_h2: Food and Drink Video Ads From Pack to Pour
steps_lead: Nutrition facts stay on the real package. Three steps take you from that photo to the clip.

steps.d: Use a clean photo of the can, bottle, or pouch, label toward the camera. Wipe fingerprints. Leave the can dry.
Name the glass, ice, and liquid color, or the plate and the bite. The hands are generated. Small print on the pack may not match.
Check the package shape and color, then download. Put allergens, ingredients, and the offer in your editor. Captions are not added for you.

steps.prompt: A hand tilts the citrus bottle and pours once into an ice-filled glass. The pour stops, and the full bottle stays beside the glass.
